title: Bounded simulation configurations
statement: Let $R$ be a natural number, let $\Lambda$ be a type of labels, let $P$ assign a counter-program instruction to each label, and fix an initial label $l_0$ and a Boolean $lm$. Let $n,B$ be natural numbers, let $u$ be a finite Boolean list, and let $o$ assign a Boolean to each pair consisting of one of two indices and a finite Boolean list. Assume that for every natural number $h$, $o$ at index $0$ on the encoding of the pair $(1^n,\operatorname{bits}(h))$ is true exactly when $h<|u|$, and $o$ at index $1$ on that encoding equals the entry of $u$ at position $h$, defaulting to false. Define the configurations $a$ that, on input $y$, are related to $y$ by the machine's pre-simulation relation and whose every register value is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ assigns an instruction to each label
$o$ has the stated two-index Boolean type
the specified condition for $o$ at index 0 holds for every $h$
the specified condition for $o$ at index 1 holds for every $h$
caveat: The precise meaning of the pre-simulation relation and pair encoding is not supplied; the statement describes their role without expanding those imported definitions.
